three assertions added by this run assert properties of the test's own expectation rather than of the code's output and therefore cannot fail: `assert expected.is_absolute()` at :467 and `assert expected.parent == Path.home().resolve()` at :468 both read `expected`, which is computed two lines above from pathlib rather than from the CLI, and the same shape appears at :494 in the relative-path test - they hold whatever router_command does and so add no protection, while the containment assertion on the following line is the one that carries the guard (the negative control failed precisely there, at :469 and :495).
